chunks.text: CVE-2021-44228 is the Log4Shell remote code execution vulnerability associated with Apache Log4j 2. This benchmark entry exists to test exact CVE identifier retrieval without confusing it with other Java vulnerabilities.

CVE-2022-22965 is commonly called Spring4Shell and affects specific Spring Framework deployments. It is intentionally similar in topic to other remote code execution advisories but has a different exact CVE identifier.
SupraCrawl Phase 3C validates real vector retrieval against OpenSearch 3.8.0. The exact release string 3.8.0 distinguishes this runtime from earlier OpenSearch releases.
OpenSearch 3.7.0 is a distinct earlier release used here only as a near-duplicate version decoy. Queries for 3.7.0 must not be silently redirected to documentation for 3.8.0.
The certified Phase 3B merge commit is 37be2292e5c4737247c940b83860a13de4ea7eb4. It records the multilingual E5-small and RRF screening experiment while leaving production BM25 unchanged.
The previous certified Phase 3A merge commit is 7488abd1101054fe65dbe685054fb5343aca852f. It represents the BM25 benchmark baseline before the Phase 3B screening experiment.
The lexical web search API is POST /v1/search. It accepts a SearchRequest containing query and limit and currently dispatches to the BM25 OpenSearch search path.
The extraction API is POST /v1/extract. It accepts URLs plus optional query, context budget, and force refresh settings and returns cleaned extracted documents.

The Phase 3B and Phase 3C candidate embedding model identifier is intfloat/multilingual-e5-small and its embedding dimension is 384. Query and passage prefixes are required by the E5 retrieval convention.
BAAI/bge-m3 is a separate multilingual embedding model with 1024-dimensional dense vectors. It is not the selected Phase 3C candidate and serves as a model-name and dimension decoy.
The OpenSearch request timeout is configured with the environment variable SUPRACRAWL_OPENSEARCH_TIMEOUT_S. It controls backend request timing and is separate from the generic fetch timeout.
The general HTTP fetch timeout is configured with SUPRACRAWL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S. This setting applies to page fetching and must not be confused with the OpenSearch backend timeout.
The IPv6 address fe80::1 belongs to the link-local fe80::/10 range and is rejected by SupraCrawl URL safety checks for outbound fetches.
The IPv4 address 127.0.0.1 is loopback localhost and is rejected by SupraCrawl SSRF validation. It is distinct from private LAN and link-local address ranges.
